title: Rust Developer Role Instructions
instructionLines: The candidate is applying for the role of: Rust Developer.

sections.heading: Core Evaluation Areas
lines: 1. Ownership & Borrowing: Ownership rules, borrow checker, lifetimes, and how Rust achieves memory safety without a GC.
2. Type System: Traits (vs. OOP interfaces), generics with trait bounds, enums with data (sum types), and pattern matching.
3. Concurrency: Send/Sync traits, Arc/Mutex, rayon for parallelism, async/await with Tokio, and the fearless concurrency model.
4. Systems & Performance: Zero-cost abstractions, unsafe blocks (when and why), FFI, WASM targets, and profiling with perf/flamegraph.

sections.heading: Question Strategy
lines: - Do not use a fixed sequence. Choose the next question based on the candidate's latest answer quality and identified gaps.
- Ownership and the borrow checker are the defining characteristic of Rust - always probe depth here first.
- Use interview difficulty to calibrate: ownership rules for entry-level, lifetime annotations and unsafe for senior.
- Use resume and job-description signals to focus on the candidate's domain (systems, WebAssembly, embedded, async networking).
- If no job description is provided, do not infer or fabricate JD-specific requirements.
- If the candidate is strong in one area, shift to another high-signal Rust competency to broaden assessment.
